metrics.rationale: User explicitly states '尽可能透过 255–280 nm 的太阳盲紫外信号' (maximize transmission of 255-280 nm solar-blind UV signal) - this is the primary passband for the detector.
User explicitly states '尽可能抑制 300–700 nm 可见光背景' (suppress 300-700 nm visible background) - this is the first rejection band requiring high reflectance/blocking.
User explicitly states '尽可能抑制 700–1100 nm 近红外杂散光' (suppress 700-1100 nm near-infrared stray light) - this is the second rejection band requiring high reflectance/blocking.

standard.metric_rationale: These three metrics directly map to the user's three explicit spectral requirements: one passband (255-280 nm UV transmission to maximize) and two distinct stopbands (300-700 nm visible and 700-1100 nm NIR to suppress). Using reflectance_stopband for the rejection bands is semantically appropriate per the catalogue guidance ('prefer this name for a rejection or stopband requirement'). I deliberately omit angle and polarization selectors since the user did not specify them, allowing default normal-incidence unpolarized evaluation. Manufacturing constraints (30 layers, no metals, dielectric materials only) are design variables handled by the optimizer, not scoring metrics. I use exactly 3 of the 4 allowed metrics to avoid diluting the comparison with unnecessary measures.
standard.formula_rationale: The user phrases all three requirements with 'as much as possible' (尽可能), indicating equal priority between maximizing signal transmission and suppressing background noise. Since all metrics are normalized fractions between 0 and 1, a direct sum assigns equal weight without introducing arbitrary coefficients. This ensures that improving any single band contributes equally to the score, while failing in any band directly penalizes the total, forcing the optimization to balance passband performance with stopband blocking.
